question: is there an art major at ramapo or just a minor
answer:
Ramapo has art majors, not just a minor: the catalog lists Communication Arts BA and Visual Arts BA as bachelor's majors in art [15]. Visual Arts also has a minor [2]. The Visual Arts BA is in the School of Arts, Humanities, and Education [2].

Sources: [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/AH-BA-ARTS) [15](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs)
note_A: Visual Arts BA (School of Arts, Humanities, and Education) and Visual Arts Minor exist in programs, so the core answer is right. But calling Communication Arts BA an art major is not supported: its catalog description and requirement groups cover only the Global Communication and Media and Digital Journalism and Writing concentrations.
note_B: programs table has Visual Arts BA (School of Arts, Humanities, and Education), Visual Arts Minor and Communication Arts BA, so 'yes, there are art majors' is supported. Calling Communication Arts an art major is a stretch, and it leaves out Visual Communication Design BA, but nothing it states is false.

question: does ramapo have anything like scientific illustration or a major that combines art and science
answer:
Ramapo lists no Scientific Illustration major in its catalog. It does offer COMM 224 FUNDAMENTALS OF ILLUSTRATION (4 credits; no published prerequisites). The catalog describes it as investigating “illustration’s capacity for personal expression within the arena of public communication,” including picture building, conceptual development, materials, and professional sharing and feedback. COMM 224 is not listed in the Visual Arts BA requirements. [2][1][5]

The catalog lists a Visual Arts BA and an Interdisciplinary Studies BA, but no specifically named art-and-science major. [5] A related option is the Visual Arts BA’s joint Art Therapy degree option: students complete the BA at Ramapo, then continue at Caldwell University for an MA in Counseling with Mental Health Counseling/Art Therapy Specialization. It combines visual arts with psychology coursework, rather than being a scientific-illustration program. [1][7]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/AH-BA-ARTS) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/COMM224) [5](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/freshmen/admission-requirements/)
note_A: No scientific illustration program is in programs. COMM 224 Fundamentals of Illustration is 4 credits with no requisites, and the quoted description matches. COMM 224 is not in the Visual Arts BA groups. The Interdisciplinary Studies BA exists, and the Visual Arts description plus the admissions page support the Caldwell art therapy joint program, whose requirement group includes PSYC courses.
note_B: No illustration program exists. COMM 224 Fundamentals of Illustration is 4 credits with no requisites, its description matches, and it is not in the Visual Arts BA groups. The Art Therapy Joint Degree Option group lists PSYC courses, and the admission-requirements page names Caldwell's MA in Counseling with the Mental Health Counseling/Art Therapy Specialization.

question: does an art class count for gen ed or do i need a specific category
answer:
You need a course approved for a specific General Education category; being an art class alone does not establish that it counts. The pages say to choose two of the three distribution categories, and to check the catalog’s approved General Education courses. [6][7][8]
Examples of art courses with Gen Ed attributes in the catalog: ARTS 206 BLACK AND WHITE PHOTOGRAPHY, ARTS 209 3D MODELING AND ANIMATION, and ARTS 214 BASIC CERAMICS are Culture & Creativity; ARTS 217 LOCAL TO GLOBAL: WORLD ANIMATION NOW and ARTS 230 REVOLUTION & LIGHT: THE ROOTS OF HAITIAN ART are Global Awareness; ARTS 219 ART AND INTERACTION is Values and Ethics. [3]
The curriculum page says take one course in two of three distribution categories: Culture & Creativity, Systems, Sustainability, & Society, and Values & Ethics; at least one must be offered by a school other than the one housing your major. [8] See the approved courses in the catalog: https://catalog.ramapo.edu/college-wide-programs/gened#general-education-categories-and-courses. [7]

Sources: [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/home/comprehensive-academic-plan/resources/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/curriculum-and-assessment/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/curriculum-and-assessment/)
note_A: The Gen Ed attributes are right: ARTS 206, 209 and 214 are GECC, ARTS 217 and 230 are GEGA, ARTS 219 is GEVE. The distribution rule matches the provost curriculum page. It repeats that page's out-of-school condition without the CAP resources page's note that this is no longer enforced from Fall 2026, but the claim is still in the data.
note_B: The Gen Ed attributes are correct: ARTS 206, 209 and 214 are GECC, ARTS 217 and 230 are GEGA, ARTS 219 is GEVE. The distribution rules match the provost curriculum page. One caveat: the CAP resources page says the out-of-school rule is no longer enforced from Fall 2026, and the answer repeats that rule without noting this.

question: what are the gen ed requirements i need to finish regardless of major
answer:
Ramapo students complete ten General Education courses: four keystone courses, one course in each of four keystone categories, and one course in two of three distribution categories. [3]

Keystone courses: First Year Seminar, Social Science Inquiry, Critical Reading & Writing 102, and Studies in the Arts & Humanities. Critical Reading & Writing 102 must be taken within the first 64 credits. [3] Another catalog page calls this course Critical Reading and Writing II. [4][9] It says reading and writing, as well as mathematics, must be completed by 64 earned credits; Banner blocks registration until Critical Reading and Writing II and general education mathematics are completed. [9]

Keystone categories: Global Awareness, Historical Perspectives, Scientific Reasoning, and Quantitative Reasoning. Quantitative Reasoning must be taken within the first 64 credits. [3]

Distribution: take one course in two of three categories. Page [3] lists Culture & Creativity, Systems, Sustainability, & Society, and Values & Ethics; page [6] lists Culture and Creativity, Values and Ethics, and Social Systems and Society, so the pages differ in the category names. Page [3] says at least one course must be offered by a school other than the one housing your major. Page [6] says that starting Fall 2026, the “out of school requirement” is no longer enforced in degree audit tools. [3][6]

Approved General Education courses: https://catalog.ramapo.edu/college-wide-programs/gened#general-education-categories-and-courses [8]

Sources: [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/curriculum-and-assessment/) [4](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#general-education) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/home/comprehensive-academic-plan/resources/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/curriculum-and-assessment/) [9](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#general-education-reading-writing-and-mathematics)
note_A: It matches the provost curriculum page: ten courses, the four keystone courses, the four keystone categories, 64-credit limits for CRWT 102 and QR, and two of three distribution categories. The catalog's 64-credit reading/writing/math policy and Banner block are paraphrased loosely but fairly. The difference in category names and the Fall 2026 non-enforcement note both match the CAP resources page.
note_B: The ten-course structure (keystone courses and categories, the 64-credit limits for CRW 102 and QR, two of three distribution categories) matches the provost curriculum page. The differing category names and the out-of-school rule no longer enforced from Fall 2026 match the CAP resources page. The Banner 64-credit block matches the catalog policy, though the answer paraphrases it loosely.

question: whats the order for the chem classes in the biochem major, like which one comes first
answer:

The chemistry sequence shown is: First Year, Spring—CHEM 117 (18 credits); Second Year, Fall—CHEM 211 and CHEM 211L (18 credits); Second Year, Spring—CHEM 213 and CHEM 213L (18 credits); Third Year, Fall—CHEM 324 and CHEM 324L, plus CHEM 425 (15.5 credits); Third Year, Spring—CHEM 350, CHEM 446, and CHEM 430 (16 credits); Fourth Year, Fall—CHEM 350L (14.5 credits). Fourth Year, Spring is 15.5 credits; the plan lists no chemistry course there. [1]

CHEM 425 is required for the major. Its prerequisites are BIOL 332 and either (CHEM 205) or (CHEM 206 and CHEM 206L), plus one of CHEM 212 or CHEM 213 and CHEM 213L. [1][3] The plan lists CHEM 425 in the same semester as BIOL 332; the prerequisites specify BIOL 332 as a prerequisite. [1][3]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BS-BCHM) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/CHEM425) [15](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs)
note_A: The Biochemistry Fall 2026 chemistry order by term is right: CHEM 116, then 117, 211, 213, then 324 and 425, then 350, 446 and 430, then 350L. But it misstates the CHEM 425 prerequisite. The data has anyOf three options: (BIOL 332 + CHEM 205), (BIOL 332 + CHEM 206/206L), or (CHEM 212 or CHEM 213/213L). The answer turns this into BIOL 332 plus organic chemistry plus CHEM 212/213, which adds requirements.
note_B: The chemistry sequence and term totals match the Biochemistry Fall 2026 plan, and CHEM 425 is in the Biochemistry BS requirements. question: can a lab science class count for both gen ed and a minor at the same time
answer:
Yes. General Education courses may double count toward a minor, up to two courses [4]. For example, GEOL 106 Fundamentals of Earth Science Lecture and GEOL 106L Fundamentals of Earth Science Lab each count for General Education Scientific Reasoning [3], and both are required for the Earth Science Minor [1]. The policy does not exclude lab science from this Gen Ed/minor double-counting allowance; its lab-science exclusion concerns credits counted toward a minor’s 16–24-credit total [5]. Check with the Office of the Provost (provost@ramapo.edu; (201) 684-7330; first floor of the Birch Mansion) about applying this to your specific course and minor [4].

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-MN-ERTH) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs) [4](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1) [5](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1)
note_A: The catalog Integrity of Degree Programs policy says students may double count up to two Gen Ed courses in a minor. GEOL 106 and 106L both carry the GESR attribute and are required for the Earth Science Minor. The lab-science exclusion is in the 16-24 credit sentence. The Provost contact details could not be found in office_sections, but they are incidental.
note_B: The catalog Integrity of Degree Programs policy says 'Students may also double count up to two General Education courses in a minor', and its lab-science exclusion applies to the minor's 16-24 credit count. GEOL 106 and 106L both carry GESR, and both are required for the Earth Science Minor. The Provost contact (provost@ramapo.edu, 684-7330) matches the provost page.

question: I work full time and want to go back for a business degree. What are the required courses for the Business Administration major, and how many credits is the major in total?

For the MBA:

- The 42-credit Program adds 6 foundational courses (2 credits each): ACCT 510 Foundations of Accounting; BADM 510 Foundation Stats for Business; ECON 510 Foundations of Economics; FINC 510 Foundations of Finance; MGMT 510 Foundations of Management; MKTG 510 Foundations of Marketing. The catalog's elective list is lengthy; see https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SB-MBA-MBAD for all options. [1] For the MBA's total credits, the catalog says 30 credits for Advanced Standing or 42 credits for the other program. [1] Undergraduate major requirements are 40–64 credits, but that rule applies to undergraduate students, not this MBA. [2]

Contact the Anisfield School of Business at asb@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7379, (201) 684-7380, or (201) 684-7378. [1]

question: How many gen ed credits does a bachelors at Ramapo require in total, and what are the categories I have to cover?
answer:
The pages do not give a fixed total number of Gen Ed credits. They say the curriculum “should not exceed 41 credits” [7]. Ramapo students take ten Gen Ed courses: four keystone courses, one course in each of four keystone categories, and one course in two of three distribution categories [10].

The four keystone courses are First Year Seminar, Social Science Inquiry, Critical Reading & Writing 102, and Studies in the Arts & Humanities. Take Critical Reading & Writing 102 within your first 64 credits [10]. The four keystone categories are Global Awareness, Historical Perspectives, Scientific Reasoning, and Quantitative Reasoning; Quantitative Reasoning must also be completed within the first 64 credits [10].

Choose two of these distribution categories: Culture & Creativity, Values and Ethics, and the third category. The pages differ on its name: “Systems, Sustainability, & Society” [9, 10] versus “Social Systems and Society” [11]. Section 10 says at least one distribution course must be offered by a school other than your major’s school; the Fall 2026 page says the “out of school requirement” is no longer enforced in degree audit tools [10, 11].

For clarification, contact the Office of the Provost: provost@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7330 [6].

Sources: [6](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#general-education) [7](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1) [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/curriculum-and-assessment/) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/home/comprehensive-academic-plan/resources/)
note_A: The catalog Integrity of Degree Programs section says Gen Ed 'should not exceed 41 credits'. The provost Curriculum section lists the ten courses: four keystone courses, four keystone categories and two of three distribution categories, with the 64-credit timing rules. The 'Systems, Sustainability, & Society' vs 'Social Systems and Society' naming and the out-of-school rule no longer enforced from Fall 2026 both match the provost pages.
note_B: No fixed Gen Ed credit total is published; Integrity of Degree Programs says it 'should not exceed 41 credits'. Provost curriculum page gives ten courses, the four keystone courses, four keystone categories (CRW 102 and QR within first 64 credits), two of three distribution categories with the out-of-school rule; CAP resources page uses 'Social Systems and Society' and says the out-of-school requirement is no longer enforced from Fall 2026.
